newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: France, U.S. asked to help S.Africans leave Congo.
newsitem.headline: France, U.S. asked to help S.Africans leave Congo.

text.p: South Africa said on Monday it had asked the United States and France to help in evacuating South African citizens from Congo.

"The South African government is seriously concerned at the heavy ongoing fighting which is reportedly continuing in Brazzaville ... between government forces and a militia group," the foreign affairs department said in a statement.
"At present a number of South African citizens, including some businessmen, are reportedly trapped in Brazzaville due to the ongoing fighting," it said.
South Africa has no resident diplomatic mission in Congo and had asked France and the United States for help in getting its citizens out of the capital.
The city was rocked by shells on Monday in fighting between government troops and supporters of ex-president Denis Sassou Nguesso.
The department said it had been in touch with a group of South African farmers living in Congo's Niari valley.
"They indicated that they did not appear to be in any danger at present," it said, adding that the situation was being monitored.
The statement called on all parties to the violence to implement a ceasefire and begin talks which would bring about lasting peace.
